Drive-in (park at your site); max trailer 30 ft / RV 34 ft, no driving restrictions. No hookups; sanitary dump station, token hot showers, sandy beach with boat rentals. Season ~late May-early Sep. Reservable online (ReserveAmerica) or FCFS for open sites. --Claude

Reservable online (ReserveAmerica) or FCFS for open sites. --Claude

was: Green Mountain National Forest (USFS), Weston. Small remote campground along Greendale Brook, ~9-11 back-in sites. First-come-first-served only (not on recreation.gov); ~$10/night. No hookups, no drinking water, vault toilet. Spurs are short -- Forest Service guidance says best for RVs under ~24 ft, so a 23-ft rig is near the upper limit; some sites take small campers/trailers/camper vans. Open seasonally (Memorial Day-Labor Day). --Claude

was: 32-site drive-in base campground at the south end of Umbagog Lake (Cambridge/Errol, NH, off Rt 26). Mix of standard, pop-up/tent, tent-only sites and 2 lean-tos; electric (15-30A) and water hookups at base, dump station, camp store, flush/pit toilets and coin showers, canoe/kayak rentals. Back-in sites; max equipment length varies 10-24 ft, so a 23-ft rig fits only the larger sites. Open Memorial Day weekend through Columbus Day weekend (2026: May 22-Oct 11). Reservable via ReserveAmerica; FCFS walk-ins also welcome. A separate 35 boat/paddle-in remote sites are NOT included here. Operator: NH Division of Parks & Recreation. --Claude

NO hookups; dump station, flush toilets, coin showers. All sites ATV-trail accessible. Season ~May 15-Oct 11. Reservable online via ReserveAmerica (some FCFS sites at campground). was: WMNF (Pemigewasset Ranger District), off NH-49 ~2 mi from I-93 exit 28. 58 sites among white pines; max RV/trailer 50 ft. No hookups or dump station; coin showers ($2.50). Open mid-May to mid-October. Mix of reservable (online/phone) and FCFS sites. --Claude

was: WMNF (Pemigewasset Ranger District), Waterville Valley. 27 sites total — 6 tent-only (no vehicles), 19 sites fit RVs/trailers ~25–30 ft (30 ft cap); a 23-ft rig fits. No hookups; vault toilets, potable water. Open mid-May to mid-October. Mix of reservable and FCFS sites. --Claude

was: WMNF (Saco Ranger District), off NH-16 ~5 mi south of Conway, base of Mt. Chocorua. 28 sites (some tent-only); fits RVs. No hookups or dump station; accessible restrooms, hand-pump water. Open mid-May to mid-October. Mix of reservable (online/phone) and FCFS sites. --Claude

was: WMNF designated roadside/dispersed camping corridor along Tripoli Rd (reached from I-93 exit 31). Drive-in numbered roadside sites managed by a concessionaire; register at the trailer on the western end. Sites range from riverside to secluded wooded; no hookups, no amenities (primitive). Open mid-May through October, FCFS only — no advance reservations. Site sizes vary — not all fit a 23-ft rig; choose a pull-through/larger pulloff. --Claude

was: WMNF (Saco Ranger District) campground on the Kancamagus Hwy (Rt 112) ~6 mi west of Conway, across from the Albany Covered Bridge. 26 sites, no hookups, vault toilets, hand-pump water; mostly level compacted-gravel pads (some former-CCC concrete pads). Sites fit RVs/trailers well over 23 ft (allstays lists up to ~65 ft; rec.gov site A045 35 ft). First-come, first-served only — NOT on recreation.gov. Season mid-May to mid-Oct. Former 1930s CCC camp with self-guided tour. --Claude

was: WMNF (Pemigewasset Ranger District), near Woodstock off Tripoli Rd. 84 sites (tent to RV); max trailer 40 ft. Flush toilets, hot showers; no on-site dump station. Open mid-May to mid-October. Mix of reservable and FCFS sites (the prime pond-side sites are FCFS-only). --Claude

was: WMNF (Pemigewasset Ranger District) campground on the Kancamagus Hwy (Rt 112), ~7 mi east of Lincoln. 28 wooded sites (sites 21-28 tent-only), each with table, tent pad and parking turnout; no hookups, no water/electric/sewer. RVs/motorhomes up to ~40 ft on most sites (8 sites share a common lot). First-come, first-served only — NOT on recreation.gov. Season mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

was: WMNF (Pemigewasset Ranger District) campground on NH Rt 112 in Easton, ~9 mi west of North Woodstock along the Wild Ammonoosuc River. 26 wooded sites, gravel pads, no hookups, vault toilets, hand-pump water; CCC picnic pavilion across the road. First-come, first-served (self-service pay) — NOT reservable on recreation.gov. FS lists max equipment length 50 ft; some reviews note tight access for larger trailers due to road/site conditions, so it suits a 23-ft rig more than big rigs. Season ~mid-May to Oct. RV Life rating is low (unrated/1*) but it is a confirmed, currently-operating WMNF campground. --Claude

was: DISPERSED drive-in camping corridor on Haystack Rd (Forest Rd off US-3, ~north of the Beaver Brook Picnic Area), Jefferson/Twin Mountain in the WMNF. 11 numbered, wooded drive-in sites, first-come-first-served, 14-night limit, up to 3 vehicles/15 people per site. Only amenity is a fire pit — no water, toilets, or trash. Seasonal: road closed in winter, opens late spring after it dries out (mid-June in some years); check the WMNF page/Facebook for status. Road ends at the Little River and the North Twin trailhead. Sites are short/rustic — fine for a 23-ft rig but verify length on arrival; not a reservation campground. --Claude

was:
Clean, well-kept RV park in Clayton minutes from Raleigh; paved streets and driveways, large patios, shady lots. Daily, weekly and monthly stays. Dogs on leash only; the park bars breeds such as German Shepherd, Pit Bull, Chow and Rottweiler. --Claude
SCREENING: the reservation request form asks whether you have ever been convicted of a felony; the park calls back to confirm. Kept as a nightly stop with a posted rate (AWH 2026-10-24). --Claude
